restated: For every P-position (p,q,r) of 3-row Chomp with r >= 1, p - q <= 3r - 1. Equivalently, for each fixed r, f(q,r) - q is at most 3r - 1 for every q >= r.
ledger_statement: CORRECTION of C0009 and (Z1). Byrnes' Lemma 5, correctly specialised to 3-row Chomp with the third row fixed, gives p - q <= 3r - 1 for EVERY P-position (p,q,r), uniformly in q. The embedding forced by Byrnes' assumption (1) is C = the row-2 tail, D = the row-1 tail, A = the 3r-1 cells of columns 1..r minus the poison, giving m = q-r and n = p-r. C0009 used n = p-q, which yields the weaker true statement (p-q)-(q-r) <= 3r-1 and a spurious (q-r) term that appears to grow with q. Consequence: (Z1) is NOT half-proved, it is fully proved in print with C = 3, and M_r <= 3r-2. The 'residual half of (Z1)' that the Phase 0 audit set as island 01's opening target does not exist.

verdicts.first_gap_line: Let (p,q,r) be a P-position with third row r. Then g(A_{m,n}) = 0 with m = q-r, n = p-r, and Lemma 5 with k = 0 gives n - m = (p-r)-(q-r) = p-q <= |A| = 3r-1.
verdicts.gap_description: The constructed A_{m,n} is not the Chomp position (p,q,r) of the cited Byrnes setting. The summands C={c_1<...<c_{m+1}}, D={d_1<...<d_{n+1}} are distinct element chains, so the embedding A u C u D has at least (3r-1)+m+n elements, whereas the actual 3-row Chomp position (p,q,r) has p+q+r-1 elements; no identification of a Chomp cell with two poset elements is established. Moreover the truncation A_{m,n} deletes all successors of c_{m+1} and d_{n+1}, which would cap every chain above them, not just the single-chain caps the computation asserts.

verdicts.effectivity_check: The bound 3r-1 is explicit and computable if the Byrnes Lemma 5 specialisation were valid; however the proof supplies no line producing a computable preperiod N(r), and its entire reduction rests on the invalid embedding. The claimed p-q <= 3r-1 does not yield N(r) by itself.
